title: Shrink a clash to a minimal one

blocks.text: The outage-week rules again. `clashing_rules(variables, rules)` is now given: it returns the names CP-SAT reports as sufficient for infeasibility, which may include rules that are not to blame. `feasible(variables, rules)` is also given: it says whether a list of rules can all hold at once.

The planners want the short list: a set of rules that clash, from which no rule can be dropped without the rest becoming satisfiable. Write `minimal_clash(variables, rules)` that returns the names of such a set, or `[]` if the rules can all hold.

Start from the names `clashing_rules` returns. Take them one at a time: if the set without that rule is still infeasible, the rule is not needed, so leave it out for good; otherwise keep it. In the notation of the previous practice, with $`S`$ the set kept so far and $`r \in S`$:
S \leftarrow S \setminus \{r\} \quad \text{if the rules in } S \setminus \{r\} \text{ have no common solution}
CP-SAT may name every rule it was given, and a scenario may hold more than one clash. About eight lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from depot_rules import Rule, minimal_clash

# Crew counts (low, high) for three depots.
crews = {"quay": (0, 5), "mill": (0, 5), "fort": (0, 5)}
all_cap = Rule("all_cap", {"quay": 1, "mill": 1, "fort": 1}, "<=", 12)
mill_max = Rule("mill_max", {"mill": 1}, "<=", 1)
mill_min = Rule("mill_min", {"mill": 1}, ">=", 3)
pair = Rule("quay_fort_min", {"quay": 1, "fort": 1}, ">=", 6)
print("all_cap, quay_fort_min, mill_max, mill_min:", minimal_clash(crews, [all_cap, pair, mill_max, mill_min]))
print("all_cap, quay_fort_min, mill_max:", minimal_clash(crews, [all_cap, pair, mill_max]))
print("all_cap at 5 with quay_fort_min, mill_min:",
      minimal_clash(crews, [Rule("all_cap", all_cap.terms, "<=", 5), pair, mill_min]))

cases.says: one clash among harmless rules comes back with no rule to spare
a scenario whose rules can all hold has no clash
when CP-SAT names every rule and two separate clashes exist, one of them comes back whole

origin.section: A Deletion Filter Shrinks the Named Flags to a Minimal Set

concepts: a deletion filter drops each rule whose removal leaves the rest infeasible
